subject: Hosted API evaluation — next steps & quickstart

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-11-18T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API evaluation — next steps & quickstart

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for your time today — great to learn more about FinTechCo's fraud-detection use case and the latency/cost targets you shared. Quick recap and next steps from the demo: 

- Hosted API looks like the simplest path for an initial eval/POC (no infra to manage, fast onboarding).
- If you need guaranteed throughput or long-term predictable unit economics we can discuss Dedicated capacity later — that would be during a pilot -> scale phase.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) is available for regulated data residency requirements but usually comes later in the procurement cycle.

Requested items I’ll send over: quickstart guide + a test API key scoped to your eval org, a short rate-limits table by plan, and a POC SOW draft. I’ve attached the Quickstart guide and will follow up with the key and sample rates.

Open questions I captured from the call:
1) Expected RPS (peak) and average monthly token volumes (estimates are fine).
2) Any data residency or strict audit/SOC2 evidence requirements for the pilot.
3) Success criteria for the POC (latency target, accuracy baseline, integration milestones).

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll provision a short-lived test key and send connection examples (curl + Python).
- You test against the Hosted API endpoints for 1–2 flows.
- If throughput looks tight we can configure autoscale for Dedicated for the pilot.

Are you ok with that plan? If yes, I’ll send the key and step-by-step quickstart later today.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0132

Hi Aditya — thanks for the recap and the demo. That plan makes sense. A few clarifications from our side before you provision the key: 

- Expected traffic for the POC: peak ~25 RPS, average ~3 RPS. Monthly token estimate ~120M tokens (we're sending both short prompts and longer context for re-ranking).
- Data residency: pilot data can live in the US. For production we may need EU residency for some customers — will flag later.
- Compliance: we do need SOC2 evidence and an audit log export capability (not necessarily before pilot, but required before any production rollout).

Specific asks: can you share the rate limits for the Hosted API (burst, sustained) and whether we can request a temporary increase for the POC? Also curious about connection examples for streaming responses and any guidance on batching for cost reduction.

If you can provide the test key and docs, Aaron and I will run an initial integration next week.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Product Lead, Risk Solutions
FinTechCo

Hi Samantha (and Aaron),

Appreciate the details — that's very helpful. Answers below and next steps: 

1) Rate limits & temporary increases:
- Default Hosted API limits: burst 50 RPS, sustained 20 RPS per org key for standard plans.
- For pilots we can grant a temporary limit increase (up to 100 RPS burst / 40 RPS sustained) for 2 weeks while you validate. I'll request that on our side; expect confirmation by EOD.

2) Token volume & batching guidance:
- For mixed short/long contexts, batching and prefix caching will reduce cost by up to ~30% depending on reuse. See the Quickstart guide (attached) — section "Batching & Caching" has code examples. 
- Streaming examples (curl + WebSocket + SDK) are in the quickstart link: https://docs.redwood.ai/hosted-api/quickstart (also linked below).

3) Compliance & audit logs:
- We can provide SOC2 report and a sample audit-log export. I'll attach the SOC2 evidence deck and include an export example in the console for the pilot. For now, note that Hosted API has audit logging for request IDs, timestamps, and user annotations.

4) Test key + endpoints:
- Test API key (scoped, short-lived): redwood_test_key_fintechco_XXXX
- Base endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Streaming endpoint: wss://stream.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream

Next steps I will do today:
- Provision test key and reply with the exact key + curl/python examples.
- Request temporary rate-limit increase and confirm.
- Share a POC SOW draft for your legal/procurement review (attached).

If all good, propose we kick the POC on Nov 23 with a 2-week validation window. Success criteria: median p50 latency < 250ms for classification/rerank flows and a baseline accuracy improvement > 5% over current heuristics. Happy to adjust.

Thanks — cc'ing Marissa from our Customer Success team to help with onboarding and post-POC transition.

Cheers,
Aditya
